tier_reason: The README table compares see::sync with tokio::sync::watch at 1/4/16/64 subscribers (84.9us vs 213.8us, 350.6 vs 388.6us, 1.52 vs 1.14ms, 2.17 vs 2.67ms) on an Intel Core i5-11300H. The Criterion code is public (benches/comparison.rs), but the rustc version is not stated beyond an unpinned nightly in flake.nix, so this is first-party partial methodology: tier C.

corrections.workload: Criterion benches/comparison.rs 'SPSC/MPSC Throughput' group, which appears to be the source of the README table (same 1/4/16/64 receiver counts): time to deliver 1,000 sends of a 1 KB payload to N receiver tasks on a tokio multi-thread Runtime, see::sync vs tokio::sync::watch
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Rust nightly (flake.nix, version unpinned); cargo bench profile defaults; Criterion 0.7
corrections.caveats: Not a uniform win: tokio is faster at 16 subscribers, and the README says so. The README does not name the bench group behind the table. The comparison runs on a tokio multi-threaded runtime, not single-threaded as first recorded (only the sync vs unsync numbers are single-threaded). The rustc version is unpinned. It measures a watch-channel sync primitive, not a reactor or event loop.

notes: Numbers match the README exactly. Repo metadata checks out: Apache-2.0 on GitHub plus LICENSE-MIT, Cargo.toml 'MIT OR Apache-2.0', 15 stars, last commit 2026-08-20, not a fork. The workload field was wrong to say single-threaded, so I fixed it.

tier_reason: The README Benchmarks section compares against uvloop with the claimed numbers: sleep(0) 4.26us vs 12.53us, lock_acquire 3.90 vs 12.26, future_res 3.91 vs 12.81, and a strace total of 1,979 vs 52,587 syscalls. The code is public (benchmarks/benchmark_suite.py, benchmarks/syscall_bench.py) and the release flags are in Cargo.toml, but no CPU model or rustc version is given anywhere (BENCHMARK.md says only 'Linux kernel 6.x'), so tier C.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Rust release profile opt-level=3, lto=true, codegen-units=1 (Cargo.toml); rustc version not stated
corrections.caveats: No CPU model; kernel given only as '6.x'. Loses to uvloop on gather(100) latency (README 139us vs 105us). The published figures disagree with each other: BENCHMARK.md lists uvloop sleep(0) at 105us and uringcore gather(100) at 156.9us, and the committed benchmarks/final_comparison.txt shows gather(100) at 188.11us for uringcore vs 116.15us for uvloop. Self-reported, dated Jan 2026.

notes: The claimed numbers match the README. The README Performance table also claims 15,394 vs 11,721 req/s against uvloop, about 1.31x (derived from page data), with no hardware stated. Metadata is correct: Apache-2.0, 2 stars, last commit 2026-01-11, active, not a fork.

tier_reason: The performance guide states Zig 0.14.0 -O ReleaseFast on an Apple M1 Pro, and comparison code exists (benchmarks/tokio_vs_zokio_direct_comparison.zig, src/bench/tokio_runner.zig). But the Tokio column is approximate ('~100M ops/sec') and not shown to come from a same-machine run, and the >50x ratios on microbenchmarks are implausible, so this is first-party and falls short of a reproducible A: tier C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Performance guide 'Tokio Baseline' ratios range from 1.52x to 96.4x: task scheduling 145M vs 1.5M ops/s (96.4x), memory allocation 16.4M vs 192K ops/s (85.4x), deep async workflows 1.4B vs ~25M (56x), await_fn 3.8B vs ~100M (38x), nested async 1.9B vs ~50M (page says 38x), async_fn creation 3.2B vs ~100M (32x), comprehensive 10M vs 1.5M (6.67x), concurrent async tasks 5.3M vs ~2M (2.65x), real I/O 22.8K vs ~15K ops/s (1.52x)
corrections.caveats: Where the Tokio baseline figures come from is unclear. Most are marked approximate. src/bench/tokio_runner.zig can generate and run a Tokio cargo bench, but it falls back to hard-coded 'literature baseline' values (task_scheduling 800K ops/s, memory_allocation 5M ops/s) that do not match the page's 1.5M/192K. Billions of ops/s for async_fn creation means sub-ns operations that were likely optimized away. The README cites an Apple M3 Pro while the guide says M1 Pro. Ratios above 50x are implausible, and realistic rows shrink to 1.5-6.7x. Treat with strong skepticism.

notes: I downgraded because the record said '32x-96x across microbenchmarks', but the same page shows 1.52x-6.67x for real I/O, comprehensive and concurrent-task rows. The tier stays C. Metadata is correct: MIT, 5 stars, last commit 2025-07-22, stale, not a fork.
